A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPIRIT, with matching authors, attack methodology, and activation-based defenses. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original jailbreak experiments, defense and utility evaluations, and appendix analyses of attack parameters and neuron selection.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds MELD emotion-recognition results and examples of defended LLaMa-Omni outputs.

M1.justification: The PGD attack, noise-sensitive-neuron selection, activation patching, fixed +1 bias addition, and neuron pruning remain unchanged. Both versions already describe clean-activation replacement and denoising when clean audio is unavailable.

E1.justification: v2 adds MELD seven-class emotion recognition, extending utility evaluation to a distinct paralinguistic task beyond transcription and open-ended audio question answering (Section 8.1, Table 4). AdvBench, AIR-Bench Chat, and LibriSpeech coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same text, clean-speech, and random-noise controls. Defense comparisons retain no defense, denoising, and white-noise addition; the new MELD evaluation reuses these comparators. Newly cited attacks are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The MELD evaluation adds Base/Instruct model configurations and accuracy reporting. Separately, audio-pruning percentages change from 1/2/3% in v1 Table 6 to 5/10/20% in v2 Table 7, while scores and Figure 2 remain unchanged. This establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 9 adds four original-versus-defended LLaMa-Omni examples, illustrating refusals and repetitive output. Existing attack-step, step-size, transcription-error, and random-versus-top-k analyses are retained, including their appendix plots.

E5.justification: v2 Table 7 adds ± terms to DSR entries that were point estimates in v1 Table 6. Existing shaded bands in Figures 6–7 are retained. The new terms are not defined, and neither run counts nor seeds are supplied, so additional repeated experiments cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v2 adds the MELD comparison and defended LLaMa-Omni outputs. Within its new Table 4, 5% LM patching scores 56.09/27.24% for Base/Instruct, versus 54.64/27.36% without defense. Audio-bias DSR at 0.1% also changes from 100.0% to 99.73%. Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Section 7.1 revises the formal activation and sensitivity expressions to use previous-layer representations and perturbations, x_n^{l-1} and delta_n^{l-1}, in place of unindexed inputs. This is a limited revision to the layerwise mathematical specification; the PGD and intervention equations remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 adds public code and evaluation results as an explicit contribution and makes the existing white-box restriction explicit in the abstract. The headline attack-success, defense-effectiveness, utility-preservation, and no-retraining claims remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 8.2 qualifies superiority over baseline defenses specifically in terms of utility. Section 8.3 adds an interpretation that interventions preserve or sometimes enhance emotion-recognition utility, although Table 4 supports this most clearly for LM patching rather than every intervention. The limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 replaces a future code-release promise and generic placeholder with a specific repository address and a stated public release. New Appendix F identifies GPT-4-0125-preview as the AIR-Bench evaluator and explains its scoring. Hardware, computation budgets, and the 10% AIR-Bench subset remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Song et al. (2025) on audio jailbreaking and Poria et al. (2019) for MELD, while removing background references to HuBERT and BLIP-2. The central positioning around speech jailbreak defenses and mechanistic interpretability is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction is rewritten with contribution bullets, the SLM background is shortened, and Appendix F adds an AIR-Bench/GPTScore explanation. Other edits clarify wording and notation; the main section sequence and most methodological and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the MELD and defended-output tables, expands Figure 1's legend and caption, and adjusts the defense table to display uncertainty. Existing appendix tables are relocated or renumbered rather than removed; Figures 2–7 retain their plots.

improvement.justification: MELD results and defended LLaMa-Omni examples broaden the evidence, while the specific code address and evaluator documentation improve reproducibility. These are useful but limited gains: the new uncertainty terms remain undefined, pruning settings are unreconciled with the retained plot, and the MELD interpretation overgeneralizes beyond the strongest configurations. The core scientific results remain largely unchanged.
